passages.provision_quote: A person, committee, or other entity shall not, during the time period set forth in subdivision (c), with malice, knowingly distribute an advertisement or other election communication containing materially deceptive content
passages.note: The duty runs against the distributor of the deceptive election communication, and the bill states that it "does not impose liability on an interactive computer service", so it places no duty on platforms.

rows.reasoning: Pellerin authored AB 2839 (2023-2024), which bars a "person, committee, or other entity" from distributing deceptive election content and expressly provides that "This section does not impose liability on an interactive computer service"; the disclosure option ("This ____ has been manipulated.") likewise falls on the candidate or advertiser. That is a duty on the speaker and distributor, not on a platform, so it does not evidence "legally require platforms to remove false information", "require platforms to label false content, rather than remove it", or any other rung on this ladder (annex hard case: a duty on the speaker, not the platform; political-ad disclaimers placed on the campaign or advertiser). No surviving passage, so the row is BLANK.
